scale.health_specificity: 0 none · 1 general sensitive data · 2 health data is sensitive w/ opt-in · 3 standalone consumer health data law
scale.private_right: 0 none · 1 limited · 2 moderate (statute or wiretap claims) · 3 broad, covers health/tracking
scale.enforcement: 0 none · 1 new law / no public actions · 2 active AG or regulator · 3 active + public settlements or suits on health/tracking
scale.tracker_coverage: 0 none · 1 implied · 2 explicit targeted ads / cookies · 3 explicit + health inference, geofencing, or sale bans

_meta.note: Directional sales guidance, not legal advice. Update via the monthly legislation-watch PR (see docs/LEGISLATION_UPDATES.md).

AL.name: Alabama
AL.penalty: Up to $15,000 per violation; permanent 45-day cure period
AL.summary: Signed April 2026. Applies to controllers processing data of 25,000+ consumers. Sensitive data, including health data, requires consent.
AL.key_risk: Low until 2027; the permanent cure period softens early enforcement.
AL.freshpaint_help: Deploying consent-gated, PHI-free routing now avoids a rebuild when the law takes effect.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.summary: No comprehensive law. Privacy bills (e.g., SB 1815) were introduced in 2026 but did not pass. HIPAA and the FTC Act apply.

CA.name: California
CA.law: CCPA / CPRA + CMIA + CIPA (amended by SB 690) + AB 45
CA.penalty: CCPA $2,500 / $7,500 intentional per violation; CIPA $5,000 statutory damages per violation; AB 45 up to $25,000 per violation
CA.hipaa_exemption: Data-level (PHI only); CMIA applies to providers
CA.summary: Most active state regulator. The AG's Healthline settlement ($1.55M, 2025) involved health-suggestive article data shared with ad partners after opt-out. AB 45 bans geofencing around health facilities. SB 690 (signed Sep 2026) ends website pen-register claims, but CIPA wiretap claims continue.
CA.key_risk: Pixels on health pages trigger CCPA opt-out / Global Privacy Control duties plus CIPA wiretap class actions at $5,000 per violation.
CA.freshpaint_help: Server-side routing honors opt-outs and GPC signals before data reaches ad platforms, and removes the browser-side third-party calls that CIPA suits target.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.penalty: Up to $20,000 per violation; cure period has ended
CO.summary: Health data is sensitive and requires opt-in consent. Universal opt-out signals must be honored. AG and district attorneys enforce; no cure period remains.
CO.key_risk: Health systems' non-PHI marketing data is fully in scope.
CO.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint gates health-inferring events on consent and honors opt-out signals server-side.

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.law: CT Data Privacy Act (CTDPA) incl. consumer health data provisions; SB 1295 (2025) & SB 4 (2026)
CT.penalty: $5,000 per willful violation (CUTPA); no cure period
CT.summary: Consumer health data rules plus a health-facility geofencing ban. 2025 amendments removed volume thresholds for anyone processing sensitive data; 2026 amendments ban sale of precise geolocation. AG publishes annual enforcement reports.
CT.key_risk: Any business processing health data is now in scope regardless of size.
CT.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint keeps consumer health data out of ad pixels unless consent is recorded.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.penalty: Up to $10,000 per violation; cure now discretionary
DE.summary: Low applicability threshold (35,000 residents). Health condition data is sensitive and requires opt-in.
DE.key_risk: No entity-level exemption, so hospital marketing data is covered.
DE.freshpaint_help: Consent-gated routing satisfies opt-in for sensitive health data.

DC.name: District of Columbia
DC.summary: A Personal Health Data Security bill is in committee. Federal HIPAA and FTC Act apply today.
DC.key_risk: Would add health-data obligations if enacted.
DC.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint keeps you ahead of a pending health-data law.

FL.name: Florida
FL.penalty: Up to $50,000 per violation (enhanced in some cases)
FL.summary: Applies only to very large controllers (about $1B+ revenue). The AG's first action was against Roku.
FL.key_risk: High penalties, but narrow scope; most relevant to national telehealth and digital health brands.
FL.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint provides a compliant analytics layer for large brands that meet FDBR thresholds.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.law: No comprehensive law; BIPA & GIPA (biometric / genetic)
IL.summary: No comprehensive privacy law, but biometric and genetic statutes give individuals a right to sue. Healthcare pixel suits here (e.g., Advocate Aurora, $12.225M) have relied on the federal Wiretap Act.
IL.key_risk: Class-action exposure rather than regulator action.
IL.freshpaint_help: Removing third-party pixels from patient journeys eliminates the disclosure that wiretap class actions are built on.

IN.name: Indiana
IN.summary: In effect since January 1, 2026. Applies at 100,000 consumers. Sensitive data, including health data, requires opt-in.
IN.key_risk: New law; no public enforcement yet.
IN.freshpaint_help: Consent-gated routing satisfies opt-in requirements for health data.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.summary: Sensitive data requires notice and opt-out rather than opt-in. One of the less stringent frameworks.
IA.key_risk: Limited exposure for HIPAA-covered entities; digital health apps face more risk.
IA.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint's opt-out-aware routing satisfies Iowa requirements.

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.summary: In effect since January 1, 2026. Requires opt-in for sensitive data and data protection assessments for targeted advertising.
KY.key_risk: New law; assessments required for ad targeting involving sensitive data.
KY.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint's routing logs support the data protection assessments the law requires.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.penalty: Up to $5,000 per violation (via state UDAP); 30-day cure through Jul 2027
LA.summary: Signed May 2026. Health and precise geolocation data require consent. No private right of action.
LA.freshpaint_help: Consent-gated routing ready before the effective date.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.summary: Strictest sale ban in the US: selling sensitive data, including consumer health data, is prohibited even with consent. Sensitive data may be processed only when strictly necessary. Bans health-facility geofencing.
MD.key_risk: Ad pixels on health pages may count as a 'sale' that consent cannot cure.
MD.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint stops health data from reaching ad platforms at all, the only safe posture under a consent-proof sale ban.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.law: None enacted; MA Consumer Data Privacy Act (S.2619 / H.5479) in conference
MA.summary: Both chambers passed versions in 2026 and a conference committee was named in June. The Senate version bans selling sensitive data; the House version includes a private right of action for large data holders. Separately, the SJC's 2024 Vita v. New England Baptist ruling held the state wiretap act does not reach web tracking.
MA.key_risk: Could become one of the strictest laws if the conference bill passes.
MA.freshpaint_help: Proactive deployment positions MA health systems ahead of a possible sensitive-data sale ban.

MI.name: Michigan
MI.summary: Comprehensive privacy bill pending in the legislature.
MI.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint ensures HIPAA compliance regardless of state-level gaps.

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.penalty: $7,500 per violation; cure period expired Jan 2026
MN.summary: No blanket exemption for HIPAA entities, so non-PHI website and marketing data is covered. Requires a data inventory and adds a right to question profiling decisions.
MN.key_risk: Hospital web analytics data is in scope.
MN.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint provides the documented data flows a Minnesota data inventory requires.

MT.name: Montana
MT.law: Montana Consumer Data Privacy Act (amended by SB 297)
MT.summary: 2025 amendments cut thresholds to 25,000 consumers and eliminated the cure period. Health data requires opt-in.
MT.key_risk: Low thresholds and no cure period.
MT.freshpaint_help: Consent-gated routing handles opt-in requirements automatically.

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.summary: Texas-style law with no revenue threshold. Health data requires opt-in.
NE.key_risk: Low exposure for HIPAA entities; applies to digital health brands.
NE.freshpaint_help: Consent-gated routing satisfies opt-in for health data.

NV.name: Nevada
NV.law: SB 370 consumer health data law (NRS 603A) + online privacy law
NV.summary: Standalone consumer health data law: consent to collect and share, written authorization to sell, and a health-facility geofencing ban. AG enforcement only.
NV.key_risk: Covers non-HIPAA health apps and advertisers.
NV.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint blocks consumer health data from ad platforms unless consent is captured.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.penalty: Up to $10,000 per violation; cure now discretionary
NH.summary: Standard comprehensive framework. Health data requires opt-in.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.law: NJ Data Privacy Act (NJDPA) + data broker/collector law A5328 (2026)
NJ.penalty: $10,000 first / $20,000 subsequent per violation; A5328 up to $50,000 per sensitive-data record sold
NJ.summary: Health data is sensitive and requires opt-in. The 2026 data collector law bans selling sensitive data and defines personal data to include cookie and pixel data. Proposed NJDPA regulations expired un-adopted in June 2026.
NJ.key_risk: Per-record penalties for selling health data via pixels.
NJ.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint keeps health data out of third-party pixels, avoiding per-record sale exposure.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.summary: 2026 bills with health-facility geofencing bans were introduced but not enacted.

NY.name: New York
NY.law: NY Health Information Privacy Act (S9269 / A10357) awaiting governor; SHIELD Act
NY.penalty: If enacted: up to $15,000 per violation (AG)
NY.hipaa_exemption: Pending bill: PHI / HIPAA entities exempt
NY.summary: A first version was vetoed in December 2025; a revised bill passed both houses in June 2026 and awaits action. It would ban selling regulated health information and covers cookie IDs, IP addresses and inferred health data. The AG already settled with NewYork-Presbyterian ($300K, 2024) over pixel tracking.
NY.key_risk: If signed, one of the toughest health-data laws in the largest US healthcare market.
NY.freshpaint_help: Proactive Freshpaint deployment positions NY entities ahead of the pending law and active AG enforcement.

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint ensures HIPAA compliance regardless of state-level gaps.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.summary: Signed March 2026. Health diagnoses are sensitive and require consent.
OK.freshpaint_help: Consent-gated routing ready before the effective date.

OR.name: Oregon
OR.law: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act (amended by HB 2008)
OR.summary: Covers health condition inferences. 2025 amendments ban selling precise geolocation and data of under-16s. Covers nonprofits; the AG publishes enforcement reports.
OR.key_risk: Broad definition of 'sale' can reach data shared with ad partners.
OR.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint blocks health condition inferences and location data from reaching ad pixels.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.law: No comprehensive law (HB 78 pending); WESCA wiretap statute
PA.summary: HB 78 passed the House in 2025 and is moving in the Senate. Meanwhile, hospital pixel class actions proceed under the state wiretap law, including a Penn Medicine settlement of up to $9.25M pending approval.
PA.key_risk: Wiretap class actions against hospital pixels.
PA.freshpaint_help: Server-side routing removes the third-party interception that WESCA claims rely on.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.law: Rhode Island Data Transparency and Privacy Protection Act
RI.penalty: Up to $10,000 per violation; no cure period
RI.summary: In effect since January 1, 2026. Thresholds as low as 10,000 residents, and every commercial website must post a privacy notice regardless of size.
RI.freshpaint_help: Consent-gated routing and documented data flows support required notices.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.penalty: $7,500 per violation, up to treble for willful; 60-day cure
TN.summary: High applicability threshold. Health data requires opt-in. Following the NIST privacy framework is an affirmative defense.
TN.key_risk: Low for health systems due to the entity exemption; relevant to digital health brands.
TN.freshpaint_help: Consent-gated routing satisfies TIPA opt-in requirements.

TX.name: Texas
TX.law: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act (TDPSA) + Texas Medical Records Privacy Act (HB 300) + SB 1188
TX.penalty: TDPSA $7,500 per violation (30-day cure); HB 300 up to $1.5M per year; SB 1188 up to $250,000 per violation
TX.hipaa_exemption: TDPSA entity-level; HB 300 reaches any entity handling PHI
TX.summary: Most aggressive state AG on privacy, including the first suit under a comprehensive state privacy law (2025) and a $1.375B Google settlement. HB 300 extends medical-records privacy duties beyond HIPAA-covered entities; SB 1188 adds EHR data-localization rules.
TX.key_risk: Large AG settlements and medical-records duties that reach non-HIPAA handlers of PHI.
TX.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint keeps PHI out of third-party trackers, the conduct Texas AG actions have targeted.

UT.name: Utah
UT.summary: Sensitive data needs only notice and opt-out. However, Utah joined the FTC's 2026 action against a telehealth brand over health-data pixels, using consumer protection law.
UT.key_risk: Consumer protection law, not the privacy act, is being used against health pixels.
UT.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint removes the pixel data flows that FTC and state UDAP actions target.

VT.name: Vermont
VT.law: Vermont Data Privacy and Online Surveillance Act (S.71)
VT.penalty: Consumer protection act penalties; 60-day cure through Jun 2029
VT.summary: Signed June 2026. Very low thresholds, consumer health data rules that apply to everyone, and a health-facility geofencing ban.
VT.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint's health-data controls will already satisfy Vermont's consumer health data rules.

VA.name: Virginia
VA.law: Virginia CDPA + SB 754 (reproductive health, 2025) + SB 338 (geolocation sale ban, 2026)
VA.penalty: $7,500 per violation (CDPA); SB 754 private actions for actual damages or $500
VA.hipaa_exemption: CDPA entity-level; SB 754 has no size threshold
VA.summary: Health data requires opt-in. SB 754 protects reproductive and sexual health data under consumer protection law with a private right of action. SB 338 bans selling precise geolocation.
VA.key_risk: Private right of action for reproductive and sexual health data.
VA.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint keeps reproductive-health page views and conditions out of ad platforms.

WA.name: Washington
WA.penalty: Consumer Protection Act: private treble damages up to $25,000 plus AG civil penalties
WA.hipaa_exemption: Data-level (non-PHI data of covered entities is in scope)
WA.summary: Broadest state health privacy law. No size threshold; separate consent to collect and to share; signed authorization to sell; geofencing ban. First private suits (e.g., against Amazon, filed 2025) are pending.
WA.key_risk: The only broad private right of action covering health-data pixels and SDKs.
WA.freshpaint_help: Freshpaint prevents consumer health data from reaching ad pixels without consent and BAA-covered routing.
